correctness.rationale: Eisele’s Proposition 2.5 computes orbit contributions using character averages. Independently reconstructed the S3 irreducible character values, both subgroup-averaging matrices, and the modular decomposition matrix D. Their sum I+Δb+6Δc=[[8,1,6],[2,3,0],[1,1,1]] has exact determinant 16, whereas D^T C D=[[14,10],[7,5]] has determinant 0. Orbit sizes 18 and 2 give 6+18+6×2+1=37. Two-sided group actions commute and X^2={0}, guaranteeing associativity. Contracted vs full monoid algebra only adds a one-dimensional Cartan block. No unsupported global lower bound is inferred.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge new explicit 37-element witness within Eisele’s established biset framework. The original construction gives a 397-element example and a general orbit-character formula, so neither the mechanism nor characteristic dependence is claimed new. Its existence alone does not imply a witness of order 37; the new orbit multiplicity choice and exact determinant constraints supply the quantitative reduction. An unpublished smaller witness or a systematic minimization hidden in earlier work remains possible.
residual_risks: Eisele’s general formula makes the 37-element specialization elementary once chosen; novelty is only the explicit substantial size reduction.

value.rationale: Substantial reduction from 397 to 37 in a natural counterexample-size question, retaining a transparent concrete group-biset construction. Smaller explicit witnesses make Cartan-determinant pathology easier to inspect, compute and compare. Not presented as a minimality theorem or a new general representation principle.

final_claim: The biset monoid of order 37 built from G=S3, one (G×G)/({1}×C2) orbit and six (G×G)/(G×C3) orbits has nonsingular ordinary Cartan matrix (determinant 16), but its characteristic-3 Cartan determinant equals 0 over the integers; no global minimum-order claim.
limitations: Full classification/minimal possible order of counterexamples is unproved; use of the general Eisele biset construction is acknowledged.
